cases.notes: Frozen RI3 relationship conformance case. Authoritative expectation is allowed only for cohorts declared production-authoritative; unsupported cohorts must fail closed.
Regression case: `use crate::target::target_fn;` in one module and a bare `target_fn()` call must bind through the item import to the one module-level symbol the path names.
Regression case: a file-level `use tokio::spawn;` stays unresolved, and `mod tests { use crate::testing::spawn; }` must not become the authoritative target of the production `spawn()` call.
Regression case: `super` inside an inline `mod tests` names the file's own module, so `use super::target_fn;` must not bind to the same-named function in the parent's parent module.

Regression case: `callee.rs` beside `callee/mod.rs`, each defining `target_fn`, leaves `use crate::callee::target_fn;` unbound. rustc rejects this layout (E0761), so no compiling form expresses the ambiguity; the live producer fails the case unless both files are indexed.
Regression case: `use crate::target::{target_fn as mint_call, Other};` then `mint_call()` must produce the same authoritative relationship identity as ci-rust-calls-02.
Regression case: a file-level `use crate::auth::target_fn;` is not in scope inside `mod tests { use crate::fakes::*; }`, so the call there must not resolve to `auth::target_fn`.

Regression case: a file-level `use crate::auth::Token;` is not in scope inside `mod tests { use crate::fakes::*; }`, so `value.target_fn()` on a `Token` parameter there must not resolve to `auth::Token::target_fn`.
Regression case: `use crate::auth::issue_token;` in workspace member `b` must never bind to member `a`'s `auth/issue_token.rs`, whose path gives the same module-key text.
Regression case: `use crate::auth::issue_token;` in workspace member `b` binds to `b`'s own item while member `a` has a same-text module.
Regression case: `auth/mod.rs` declares both `pub mod target_fn;` and `pub fn target_fn()`, so `use crate::auth::target_fn;` binds no call target.
Regression case: `let handle = Server::spawn();` where `spawn` returns `ServerHandle` must not type `handle` as `Server`, so `handle.shutdown()` has no authoritative edge to `Server::shutdown`.
Regression case: a block `use crate::b::target_fn;` shadows the file-level `use crate::a::target_fn;`; when the block import is unresolved, the call must not fall back to `a::target_fn`.
Regression case: with `#[path = "auth_v2.rs"] mod auth;`, a stale `src/auth.rs` is not the module `crate::auth` names.
Regression case: `legacy/session.rs` mounted by `#[path]` as `crate::session` must not resolve `use super::target_fn;` to `legacy::target_fn`.
Regression case: a call inside `mod tests { use super::*; }` binds through the file-level `use crate::target::target_fn;`, which the glob names.

Regression case: `mod tests { use super::*; use crate::fakes::*; }` could take `target_fn` from either glob, so the call must not bind to the parent's import. rustc rejects the call as ambiguous; the index must still fail closed.

Regression case: the file's own `target_fn` is not in scope inside `mod tests { use mock_clock::target_fn; }`, so the call there must not bind to it; the import is unresolved and the call gets no authoritative edge.

Regression case: `Client` in `caller_fn` names the unresolved `use reqwest::Client;`, so neither `Client::new()` nor `client.target_fn()` may bind to `fakes::Client` declared in a sibling `mod` block of the same file.
Regression case: `mod tests { use super::*; }` brings the file's own `target_fn` into scope, so the call inside it binds to that item.
Regression case: a call inside a `mod` block binds to an item the block itself declares, with no import.
Regression case: `mod tests { use crate::clock::target_fn; }` names the call's target; the file's own `target_fn` is not in scope inside the block.
Regression case: `mod tests { use super::*; }` brings the file's own `Token` into scope, so a method call on a `Token` parameter there binds to `Token::target_fn`.
Regression case: `mod tests { use super::target_fn; }` names the file's own `target_fn`, so the call inside the block binds to it.

Regression case: `mod tests { use super::*; use proptest::prelude::*; }` still binds the call to the file's own `target_fn`; a second glob supplying the name too would make the call ambiguous and fail to compile.

Regression case: a bare `target_fn()` inside a method of `impl Session` does not name the associated `Session::target_fn`; with the name imported from a crate the index does not hold, the call gets no authoritative edge.
Regression case: a bare `target_fn()` inside a method binds through `use crate::clock::target_fn;`, not to the associated `Session::target_fn` of the enclosing `impl`.

Regression case: `super::target_fn()` inside `mod tests` of `src/worker.rs` names the file's own `target_fn`. The path used to climb from the file path to the crate root, losing this edge and proving one to the crate root's `target_fn` instead.

Regression case: `super::target_fn()` inside `mod tests` names the file's `use mock_clock::target_fn;`, which the index does not hold, so the call gets no authoritative edge; the crate root's `target_fn` must not take it.
Regression case: `self::target_fn()` inside `mod tests` names the item the block declares.
Regression case: `self::target_fn()` inside `mod tests` names the block's unresolved `use mock_clock::target_fn;`, so the call must not bind to the file's own `target_fn`.
Regression case: `super::target_fn()` inside `mod inner` names the item of the enclosing `mod outer`, not anything the file path climbs to.
Regression case: `super::super::target_fn()` inside `mod tests` of `src/worker.rs` leaves the block, then the file, and names the crate root's `target_fn`.

Regression case: `self::child::target_fn()` in `src/lib.rs` names `target_fn` in `src/child.rs`, the file `mod child;` declares; the scope the parser gives the bodiless declaration is not the module's body.
Regression case: `super::child::target_fn()` inside `mod tests` of `src/lib.rs` leaves the block for the crate root and names `target_fn` in `src/child.rs`, the file `mod child;` declares.
Regression case: `self::target_fn()` inside `mod tests { use super::*; }` names the file's own `target_fn`, which the glob brings into the block's namespace.

Regression case (#526): inside `mod tests { use mock_clock::target_fn; }` the file's own `target_fn` is not in scope, so no CALLS edge of any authority may link the call to it, including the symbol-registry pass's same-file edge, which reaches get_references callers and impact's possible impact.
Regression case (#526): an item of a sibling `mod` block is not in scope by its bare name, so no CALLS edge of any authority may link the call to it.

Regression case (#535): `#[path = "elsewhere.rs"] mod pathed;` in `src/w.rs` compiles `src/elsewhere.rs`, so `self::pathed::target_fn()` must not prove an edge to the `src/w/pathed.rs` left at the default location.
Regression case (#535): `crate::w::pathed::target_fn()` must not prove an edge to `src/w/pathed.rs` when `w` declares `pathed` with `#[path]`.

Regression case (#535): in `legacy/session.rs` mounted by `#[path]` as `crate::session`, `super::target_fn()` names the crate root's item, so no edge may be proven to `legacy::target_fn` from the file path.

Regression case (#542): in workspace member `crates/a` of a root package, `crate::only_root::target_fn()` names a module only the root package declares, so no edge may be proven into the root package's `src/only_root.rs`.
Regression case (#542): `crate::util::target_fn()` in workspace member `crates/a` names the member's own `util.rs`, not the root package's same-text module.
Regression case (#542): `src/bin/tool.rs` is a crate root of its own, so its `crate::x::target_fn()` must not prove an edge to the library's `src/x.rs`.
Regression case (#543): `pub mod r#type;` is the file `src/type.rs`, so `crate::r#type::target_fn()` proves an edge to its `target_fn`.
Regression case (#543): with `[lib] path = "src/app_lib.rs"`, that file is the crate root, so `crate::a::target_fn()` proves an edge to `src/a.rs`, the file its `mod a;` declares.
Regression case (#542 review): `src/bin/multi/main.rs` is a crate root whose `mod inner;` is `src/bin/multi/inner.rs`, so `self::inner::target_fn()` proves an edge to it.
Regression case (#542 review): `mod sub;` in the crate root `src/bin/tool.rs` is `src/bin/sub/mod.rs`, so `crate::sub::target_fn()` proves an edge there and not to `src/bin/tool/sub.rs`.
Regression case (#542 review): `mod common;` in the integration test `tests/it.rs` is `tests/common/mod.rs`, so `crate::common::target_fn()` proves an edge to it.

Regression case (#542 review): `tests/support/util.rs`, mounted by `#[path]` from the integration test `tests/a.rs`, calls `crate::target_fn()`; no edge may be proven into the unrelated test crate `tests/c.rs`, which defines its own `target_fn`.

Regression case (#554): `src/main.rs` is not indexed (`.okignore`), and only it declares `mod cli;`, so `crate::target_fn()` in `src/cli.rs` must not prove an edge to the library's `target_fn` in `src/lib.rs`.

Regression case (#554): no crate root declares `src/bin/tool/sub.rs` (`mod sub;` in `src/bin/tool.rs` would be `src/bin/sub.rs`), so `use crate::target_fn;` there must not bind the binary's `target_fn`.
Regression case (#544): `[[bin]] path = "src/cli.rs"` is a crate root, so `crate::util::target_fn()` from it proves an edge to `src/util.rs`, which only that root declares.

Regression case (#561): `[lib] path = "lib.rs"` and `[[bin]] path = "main.rs"` both declare `mod util;`, so `crate::target_fn()` in `util.rs` names the library's `target_fn` in one crate and the binary's in the other; no edge may be proven to either.

Regression case (#561): with `[lib] path = "lib.rs"` beside `[[bin]] path = "main.rs"`, `util.rs` is declared by the library alone, so `crate::target_fn()` there proves an edge to the library's `target_fn`.

Regression case (#572): `[lib] path = "src/../lib.rs"` is the `lib.rs` beside `[[bin]] path = "main.rs"`, and both declare `mod util;`, so `crate::target_fn()` in `util.rs` names a different function in each crate; no edge may be proven to either.

Regression case (#572): `src/lib.rs` is not indexed (`.okignore`) and, like `src/main.rs`, declares `mod util;`, so `crate::target_fn()` in `src/util.rs` must not prove an edge to the binary's `target_fn`.

Regression case (#572): `src/lib.rs` declares `mod util;` and `src/main.rs` mounts the same file with `#[path = "util.rs"] mod u2;`, so `crate::target_fn()` in `src/util.rs` names a different function in each crate; no edge may be proven to either.

Regression case (#587): `use engine::target_fn;` in a package whose manifest declares `engine.workspace = true`, read from `[workspace.dependencies] engine = { path = "crates/engine" }`, binds the call to that crate's item, not to the `target_fn` of another workspace's package also named `engine`.
Regression case (#587): `use engine::api::target_fn;` reaches the item through `pub use crate::inner::target_fn;` in the dependency's `api` module.
Regression case (#587): `use engine::target_fn;` reaches the item through the dependency crate root's glob re-export `pub use inner::*;`.
Regression case (#587): `engine::inner::target_fn()` with no `use` resolves in the declared dependency's library.
Regression case (#587): a package that does not declare `engine` must not bind `use engine::target_fn;` to a workspace sibling named `engine`.
Regression case (#587): `engine = "1"` is a registry dependency; the repository's own package named `engine`, outside the caller's workspace, must not take the edge.
Regression case (#587): with `core_alias = { package = "engine", path = "../engine" }`, code writes `core_alias`, so `use engine::target_fn;` names no crate of the repository.
Regression case (#587): the renamed dependency's items bind under its new name, `use core_alias::target_fn;`.
Regression case (#587): `engine::target_fn()` with no `use` is a path through the declared crate and resolves at its root.

Regression case (#587): `|engine| engine.target_fn()` calls a method of a closure parameter, which has the receiver text of `engine::target_fn()` and no recorded binding; it must not reach the declared `engine` crate's `target_fn`.
Regression case (#587): the same through `if let Some(engine) = first { engine.target_fn(); }`.

Regression case (#587): inside package `engine`'s own library, `|engine| engine.target_fn()` must not reach the crate root's `target_fn`: library code cannot name its own crate, and a value is no path.

Regression case (#593): `PlanEngine::target_fn("index")` reaches the associated function declared in `impl<'a> PlanEngine<'a>`, whose members belong to `PlanEngine` and not to the written type `PlanEngine<'a>`.

Regression case (#593): `self.target_fn()` in a method of `impl<T> Wrapper<T>` reaches the `target_fn` declared there: `self` is a `Wrapper`, not the written type `Wrapper<T>`, and the method is a member of `Wrapper`.
Regression case (#593): `PlanEngine::target_fn("index")` through `use engine::PlanEngine;` reaches the associated function of the dependency crate's `impl<'a> PlanEngine<'a>`.

Regression case (#593): `impl Wrapper<u8>` and `impl Wrapper<u16>` each declare `target_fn`, and the index does not match type arguments, so `self.target_fn()` in `impl Wrapper<u8>` keeps both candidates and emits no authoritative edge.

Regression case (#576): `src/main.rs` is not indexed (`.okignore`) and may declare `mod a;` as `src/lib.rs` does, so `src/a.rs` may be compiled into both crates; `self::inner::target_fn()` there ends below `a`, in `src/a/inner.rs` in every crate that declares `a`, and proves the edge.
Regression case (#576): the layout of `-75`, with the call in `mod tests` of `src/a.rs`: `super` leaves the block for `a`, and `super::inner::target_fn()` ends below it in `src/a/inner.rs`.

Regression case (#576): `tests/it.rs` mounts the library's `src/sub/mod.rs` with `#[path]`, so rustc compiles the `src/sub/child.rs` it declares into the test crate too, and `crate::target_fn()` there names a different function in each crate; no edge may be proven to either.

Regression case (#599): `w.target_fn()` on a parameter annotated `&Wrapper<u8>` reaches the method of `impl<T> Wrapper<T>`: the annotation is a `Wrapper`, seen through the reference and without its generic arguments.
Regression case (#599): `w.target_fn()` on `let mut w: Wrapper<u8>` reaches the method of `impl<T> Wrapper<T>`.

Regression case (#599): `things: Vec<Thing>` is a `Vec`, so `things.target_fn()` is the extension trait's method on `Vec`, never `Thing`'s same-named method; stripping generic arguments must not type the receiver as the element type.

Regression case (#599): `impl Wrapper<u8>` and `impl Wrapper<u16>` each declare `target_fn`, and the index does not match type arguments, so `w.target_fn()` on `w: &Wrapper<u8>` keeps both candidates and emits no authoritative edge.

Regression case (#599): `crate::engine::PlanEngine::target_fn()` reaches the associated function of the `PlanEngine` that `src/engine.rs` declares: the path's last segment names a type of the module the rest of the path reaches.
Regression case (#599): `engine::PlanEngine::target_fn()` with no `use` reaches the associated function of the `PlanEngine` at the root of the declared dependency crate `engine`.

Regression case (#599): `crate::engine::PlanEngine::target_fn()` names `PlanEngine`, which declares no `target_fn`; the same-named associated function of another type in that module must not take the edge.

Regression case (#599): `|w: &Wrapper<u8>|` binds `w` in the closure alone, so `w.target_fn()` after the closure is a call on the function's `w: Vec<Thing>` and must not reach `Wrapper`'s `target_fn`.

Regression case (#604): `tests/it.rs` mounts the library's `src/sys/mod.rs` with `#[path]`, and that file declares `#[cfg_attr(unix, path = "unix.rs")] #[cfg_attr(windows, path = "windows.rs")] mod imp;`, so rustc compiles `src/sys/unix.rs` into the test crate too on the configurations that select it, and `crate::target_fn()` there names a different function in each crate; no edge may be proven to either.

Regression case (#608): `tests/it.rs` mounts the library's `src/sys/mod.rs` with `#[path]`, and that file declares `#[cfg_attr(windows, path = "../common.rs")] mod imp;`, so on every other configuration rustc compiles `imp` from its default location, `src/sys/imp.rs`, into the test crate too, and `crate::target_fn()` there names a different function in each crate; no edge may be proven to either.

Regression case (#608): `src/sys/mod.rs` declares `#[cfg_attr(windows, path = "win.rs")] mod imp;`, so unless the condition holds `imp` is compiled from `src/sys/imp.rs`, whose `super::target_fn()` names `sys`'s `target_fn`.
Regression case (#613): `#[cfg_attr(all(), path = "x.rs")] pub mod imp;` holds on every build, so `crate::sys::imp::target_fn()` must not reach the leftover `src/sys/imp.rs`, which is never compiled.

Regression case (#613): `cfg_attr(unix, path = "u.rs")` beside `cfg_attr(not(unix), path = "o.rs")` covers every build, so `crate::sys::imp::target_fn()` reaches `u.rs` and `o.rs` (two candidates, neither authoritative) and never the leftover `src/sys/imp.rs`.

Regression case (#613): `#[cfg_attr(windows, path = "win.rs")] pub mod imp;` beside `src/sys/imp.rs` gives `imp` two files, so `crate::sys::imp::target_fn()` keeps a candidate in each and no authoritative edge.

Regression case (#613): `#[cfg(not(windows))] pub mod imp;` beside `#[cfg(windows)] #[path = "win.rs"] pub mod imp;` gives `imp` two files, so `crate::sys::imp::target_fn()` keeps a candidate in each and no authoritative edge.

Regression case (#613): `self::inner::target_fn()` in `src/sys/imp.rs`, the default location of a `cfg_attr` path module, names `src/sys/imp/inner.rs`: that file is compiled only when `imp` is, so the choice is already made.
